answer: Make identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit and build a public history of useful work before it can earn. A fake account then faces a slow glacier of cost — deposits, compute, and reputation built over weeks — while the honest signal of consistent, attested work rises above the noise. When a tide of fresh sybils arrives, rate limits tied to stake and history throttle them, and peers weight votes by proven track record, not raw headcount, so flooding the network buys influence only at a price that grows with every fake identity.
